recall_prompt: Say how you would resolve (2x² + 3x + 4)/((x − 1)(x² + 2)) into partial fractions — name each move in order.
insider_note: x² + 2 has no real factors, so its numerator must be Bx + C, never a constant; after x = 1 gives A, the easy value x = 0 gives C, and only B needs a coefficient comparison.

steps.label: Set up the form
steps.margin_note: First mark. x² + 2 has no real factors (x² = −2 has no real solution), so it is an irreducible quadratic and gets the numerator Bx + C. The linear factor gets A.

recall.must_convey: That x² + 2 is irreducible and the form is A/(x − 1) + (Bx + C)/(x² + 2).
accept: x squared plus two cannot be factorised so write A over x minus one plus Bx plus C over x squared plus two
linear factor gets a constant, the quadratic gets Bx plus C
A by x minus 1 plus Bx plus C by x square plus 2
x square plus two ki real factors levu, kabatti A by x minus one plus Bx plus C by x square plus two ani rasali
the quadratic factor is irreducible so its numerator is linear

steps.why: The numerator over a quadratic must be one degree lower, so linear. Bx + C carries two unknowns, and together with A that gives three, matching the three coefficients of the quadratic identity that follows.
common_mistakes: Writing a constant B over x² + 2.
Trying to factorise x² + 2 as (x + √2)(x − √2) with irrational factors; the form asked for uses the real quadratic as it is.
Writing (Bx + C)/(x − 1) and A/(x² + 2), swapping the numerators.

steps.label: Clear the denominators
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply by (x − 1)(x² + 2). A keeps (x² + 2), (Bx + C) keeps (x − 1). Keep Bx + C in a bracket.

recall.must_convey: That multiplying through gives 2x² + 3x + 4 = A(x² + 2) + (Bx + C)(x − 1).
accept: multiply both sides by x minus one into x squared plus two to get two x squared plus three x plus four equals A into x squared plus two plus Bx plus C into x minus one
clear the denominators so A keeps x squared plus two and Bx plus C keeps x minus one
multiply through by the whole denominator to get an identity in x
denominator tho multiply cheste A into x square plus two plus Bx plus C into x minus one vastundi
remove the fractions by multiplying with x minus one times x squared plus two
heard_as: A into x squared plus two
Bx plus C into x minus one

steps.why: One line turns the fraction equation into a polynomial identity. From here one substitution and two coefficient comparisons are enough, because both sides are quadratics.
common_mistakes: Writing Bx + C(x − 1) without the bracket.
Giving A the factor (x − 1) instead of (x² + 2).

steps.label: Find the constants
steps.margin_note: Third mark. x = 1 gives A directly. x = 0 is not a root but it is an easy value: it gives 2A − C, hence C. Then compare x² for B. The book uses exactly these three lines.

recall.must_convey: That x = 1 gives A = 3, x = 0 gives 4 = 2A − C so C = 2, and comparing x² gives A + B = 2 so B = −1.
accept: put x equals one to get A equals three, x equals zero to get four equals two A minus C so C is two, compare x squared to get B equals minus one
A is three from the root, C is two from x equals zero, B is minus one from the x squared coefficient
A three C two B minus one
x equals one pedithe A three, x equals zero pedithe C two, x square compare cheste B minus one
one root, one easy value and one coefficient give the three constants

steps.why: Any value of x may be put into an identity, not only roots. x = 0 is chosen because it makes Bx vanish and leaves a one-line equation in A and C. The x² comparison then gives B from A.
common_mistakes: Putting x = 0 and writing (0 + C)(0 − 1) as +C instead of −C, so C comes out as −2.
Writing B = 2 by forgetting A in the x² coefficient.

steps.label: Write the result
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Bx + C = −x + 2, written as 2 − x. Write the original fraction on the left.

accept: the answer is three over x minus one plus two minus x over x squared plus two
three by x minus one plus two minus x by x square plus two
B is minus one and C is two so the numerator is two minus x
final answer three by x minus one plus two minus x by x square plus two ani rasali
put A B and C back to get three over x minus one plus minus x plus two over x squared plus two

steps.why: The resolved form with the linear numerator −x + 2 in place is the marked answer. Writing it as 2 − x is neater and is how the book prints it.
common_mistakes: Not checking: put x = 2 in the identity, 18 = 18 + 0. If the two sides differ, a constant is wrong.
